FN-NY7XJ8J-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 149
Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/19/2024
Senate Bill 149 as introduced would increase the obligations of the State General Fund by an
estimated $1.0 million in fiscal year 2024 and $4.0 million in fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal
year there after to increase the daily rate for the feeding of prisoners in county jails from $2.25
per day to $3.00 per day. In addition, this bill would increase the amount that may be requested
from the Emergency Prisoner Feeding Fund by sheriffs and county commissions for cost
overruns from $25,000 to 50,000, which could increase the obligations of the Emergency
Prisoner Feeding Fund. However any increased obligations to this Fund would be offset by an
undetermined amount, up to a maximum of $250,000 in fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year
thereafter, depending on the ending balance of the Emergency Prisoner Feeding Fund at the end
of the immediately preceding fiscal year from the increase in the annual State General Fund
appropriation provided pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Further, this bill would authorize a sheriff or county commission to use funds from any source
for feeding of prisoners and would prohibit the Department of Finance from considering other
funds transferred to the sheriff for feeding prisoners when validating a cost overrun.

FN-NY7XJ8J-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 149
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/16/2024
Senate Bill 149 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of the State General Fund
as shown below by increasing the daily rate for feeding of prisoners from $2.25, under current
law, to $3.00 by increasing the rate by $0.25 each fiscal year 2025, 2026, and 2027:
Fiscal Year Daily Rate Amount
2025 $2.50 $1.3 million
2026 $2.75 $2.6 million
2027 and annually thereafter $3.00 $3.9 million
In addition, this bill would increase the amount that may be requested from the Emergency
Prisoner Feeding Fund by sheriffs and county commissions for cost overruns from $25,000 to
50,000, which could increase the obligations of the Emergency Prisoner Feeding Fund. However
any increased obligations to this Fund would be offset by an undetermined amount, up to a
maximum of $250,000 in fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter, depending on the
ending balance of the Emergency Prisoner Feeding Fund at the end of the immediately
preceding fiscal year from the increase in the annual State General Fund appropriation provided
pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Further, this bill would authorize a sheriff or county commission to use funds from any source
for feeding of prisoners and would prohibit the Department of Finance from considering other
funds transferred to the sheriff for feeding prisoners when validating a cost overrun.
